terms.plainEnglish: Creates a variable name that cannot be reassigned to a different value.
terms.confusion: The value can still be mutable. For example, a const array can still have items pushed into it.

terms.plainEnglish: Creates a variable whose value can be reassigned later.
terms.confusion: Use let when the value really needs to change; otherwise const is usually clearer.

terms.plainEnglish: Defines a reusable block of code that can be called by name.
terms.confusion: Defining a function does not run it. The function runs only when it is called.

terms.plainEnglish: Marks a function as asynchronous, so it returns a Promise.
terms.confusion: Async does not make code run on a separate thread. It helps work with operations that finish later.

terms.plainEnglish: Pauses an async function until a Promise settles, then gives back the result.
terms.confusion: Await can only be used in async functions or in modules that support top-level await.

terms.plainEnglish: Creates a new array by transforming each item in an existing array.
terms.confusion: Map is for changing each item into a new value, not for filtering items out.

terms.plainEnglish: Creates a new array containing only the items that pass a true-or-false test.
terms.confusion: Filter keeps or removes whole items. It does not transform the kept items.

terms.plainEnglish: Combines array items into one result, such as a total, object, or grouped value.
terms.confusion: Reduce can be powerful but hard to read. For beginners, a loop is sometimes clearer.

terms.plainEnglish: Starts a network request and returns a Promise for the response.
terms.confusion: Fetch does not directly return the final data. You usually need to call response.json() or response.text().
